soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 (compatibility frontier), including its use as the project headline
soundness_flags.one_line: The advertised iff is largely the definition of Pi_S plus the block-diagonal completion construction, so it carries only one-to-two substantive steps and cannot by itself support flagship framing.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 3 (calibration-design frontier)
soundness_flags.one_line: After W_pi and Theta_H are defined, the hitting-set iff is a direct quantifier rewrite of compatibility and tuple-set equality rather than a separate structural characterization.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 1 through Theorem 4
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: All population claims are conditional on the restrictive component-aligned jointly Gaussian LiMVAM class with positive-definite coordinate disturbance stacks.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Exact compatibility and calibration conclusions hold only within the component-aligned Gaussian completion class, not for the published LiMVAM class generally.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 5
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Coverage and exact poset recovery are conditional on common-target calibration-plus-marginals sampling and the two positive away-from-strata margins.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The stated finite-sample guarantees hold under the named sampling design and feasibility/path-product separation conditions.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 2 requires an edgewise within-view correlation and a difference between the cause's cross-view correlation and the effect disturbance's cross-view correlation; Theorem 3 identifies the partial order and all B_i, while Assumption 3 identifies P.
Lemma 1 characterizes an exogenous variable through independence from pairwise-regression residuals; Lemma 2 closes LiNGAM after removal and Corollary 1 preserves the remaining order.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 4-6, Lemma 2, Theorem 1, and finite-sample Assumption 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses precision-matrix Schur-complement updates after terminal-node removal and explicit finite-sample precision-entry and terminal-score gaps.
The paper constructs estimators and confidence regions for identified sets by inversion of a sample criterion and develops consistency and rate results.
The paper recursively enumerates MPDAG subclasses whose total effects are distinct functionals, avoiding causal duplicates.
The paper gives a linear-delay algorithm for enumerating graph-distinct DAGs in a Markov equivalence class.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the headline fixed-order completion with a genuinely nontrivial transfer result: characterize a generic algebraic region of calibration designs on which a proper subset is sufficient, including an explicit exceptional variety and a strict comparison to full pairing.

Promote the omitted calibration-graph problem: give a necessary-and-sufficient positive-definite completion criterion for arbitrary observed view-pair graphs, with a nonchordal obstruction or a constructive decision procedure.

Keep the current clique result as a supporting proposition and sharpen the output-sensitive OEQ into a theorem target with a precise oracle model, lower-bound route, and a worked tuple-duplicate family that defeats path enumeration.

recommended_next_step: Revise the flagship framing around a non-definitional partial-calibration phenomenon; retain the current clique frontier, recursion, and inversion results as supporting field-level infrastructure.
